Title: M:N Free Sewing
Content: List of Contents M: N Free Sewing Create M: N Free Sewing Delete vs Esc Unlink M: N Sewing M: N Free Sewing - Freely create Sewing Lines to sew multiple Patterns to multiple Patterns at once. - Hold down the Free Sewing tool to access the child menu. Click the M: N Free Sewing tool. - Or, navigate to the Main Menu and select Sewing M: N Free Sewing. Create M: N Free Sewing - When the M: N Free Sewing tool is selected, a comment will appear next to the mouse cursor guiding to begin creating M Sewing Lines. - Establish the start and end points on the Pattern outlines that belong to M Sewing Lines. To complete the M Sewing Lines, hit the Enter key on the keyboard. - A comment will appear next to the mouse cursor guiding to begin creating N Sewing Lines. - Repeat the same process as creating the M Sewing Lines. - Hit the Enter key on the keyboard to complete M: N free Sewing Lines. Delete vs Esc - Delete: hit the Delete key on the keyboard to cancel the latest action. - Esc: hit the Esc key on the keyboard to cancel the entire action. Unlink M: N Sewing - Select the Edit Sewing tool from the 2D toolbar. - Right-click on the Sewing Line and select Unlink M: N Sewing from the pop-up menu. - The selected M: N Sewing Lines will be unlinked and they can be edited individually.

Title: M:N Segment Sewing
Content: List of Contents M: N Segment Sewing Create M: N Segment Sewing Delete vs Esc Unlink M: N Sewing M: N Segment Sewing - Create Segment Sewing Lines to sew multiple Patterns to multiple Patterns at once. - When the length of M Sewing Lines is different from the length of the N Sewing Lines, N Sewing Line length will be divided in proportion to M Sewing Lines. - Hold down the Segment Sewing tool to access the child menu. Click the M:N Segment sewing tool. - Or, navigate to the Main Menu and select Sewing M: N Segment Sewing. Create M: N Segment Sewing - When the M:N Segment Sewing tool is selected, a comment will appear next to the mouse cursor guiding to begin creating M Sewing Lines. - Click on the Pattern outlines that belong to M Sewing Lines. To complete the M Sewing Lines, hit the Enter key on the keyboard. - A comment will appear next to the mouse cursor guiding to begin creating N Sewing Lines. - Repeat the same process as creating the M Sewing Lines. - Hit the Enter key on the keyboard to complete M: N Segment Sewing Lines. Delete vs Esc - Delete: hit the Delete key on the keyboard to cancel the latest action. - Esc: hit the Esc key on the keyboard to cancel the entire action. Unlink M:N Sewing - Select the Edit Sewing tool from the 2D toolbar. - Right-click on the Sewing Line and select Unlink M: N Sewing from the pop-up menu. - The selected M: N Sewing Lines will be unlinked and they can be edited individually.

Title: Add/Apply Grading
Content: List of Contents Add Grading Apply Grading Grading Properties Add and Apply patterns of multiple sizes. Add Grading Click the button in the Grading tab in the Object Browser. Click the Add Size button next to Size Group to add a new size to the group. Note: Open the RUL file corresponding to the pattern by clicking Open Grade Rule on the right side of the Size Group. In Size Groups, you can add/insert smaller sizes or sizes in between at any point. Right-click on a size in a size group, and then click the Insert 1 Size Above menu. For adding bigger sizes, click the Add Size button next to Size Group. Apply Grading Click the 2D pattern using the Transform Pattern or Edit Pattern tool in the 2D toolbar. Click Assign to Selected Pattern button next to Size Group. Or Click button to assign to new grading rule. Grading Properties Click the Size Group. Set the following properties. Properties Description Name Set the name of the Size Group and Size. Show Shows or hides the grading segments displayed in the 2D pattern.

Title: Buttonhole Properties
Content: Adjust buttonhole properties such as Transformation and 2D Measurements. Click on the Buttonhole using the Select/Move Button tool in the 3D toolbar. Adjust the Buttonhole properties. Option Description Style Select a buttonhole style. Buttonhole Transformation Angle Enter the desired value for Rotation Angle of buttonholes. Z-Offset Even when the buttonhole is hidden due to additional thickness and displacement maps on fabrics, adjusting the Z-Offset can make it visible. Bind Position Change the bind position of the buttonhole by percentage (%). It can also be entered in units of the program setting. 2D Measurement Check the position of the buttonhole in the 2D pattern (left/right/top/bottom) with Measurement.

Title: Human IK – Edit Full Body/ Edit Body Part
Content: Human IK - Edit Full Body/Edit Body Part - Decide how to move and rotate Avatar joints. Only one option can be used at a time. Edit Full Body - When moving and rotating a single joint, all others joints will be modified as well to create an organic pose. Edit Body Part - When moving and rotating a single joint, only directly connected joints will be modified.

Title: [Style Property] Button
Content: Change color and texture of buttons as desired. Click the Button style in Button tab in Object Browser. Adjust the properties referring to the following as needed. Options Desciption Information Name/ Item NO. Enter a name and an item number of the button. Tech Pack (CLO-SET) Set whether you include the button in the Tech Pack or not. Shape Thread Type Set the type of thread (Cross, Parallel, Square) Width Set the width of the button. User Settings User setting you can change the button unit to L. Link to Fastend Buttonhole(ver 2024.1) If the button is fastened, you can automatically apply the width change to the fastened buttonhole as well. Thickness Set the thickness of the button. Weigh Set the weigh of the button. Material Set the Material of the button. If you turn off Use Same Material as Button option in the Thread tab, you can set those materials separately. You can apply metal easily with the newly provided metal presets.

Title: Does CLO offer refunds?
Content: Unfortunately, we do not offer refunds as stated within CLO's Terms of Service agreement. Please note that CLO provides auto-renewal subscriptions for individual users, showing a clear notification on the checkout page and asking for your consent before you purchase CLO, as shown below. *Auto-renewal and cancellation policy Once you are subscribed, you will be automatically billed and charged every term based on your choice (monthly or yearly). You can cancel your subscription anytime on your Subscription page, which will stop future billings, and give you account access through the end of your current term. The cancellation will take effect at the end of the current subscription term youve already been billed. Consequently, you wont receive any refunds for the remaining duration of your subscription term after youve cancelled. Upon cancellation of your subscription, you will receive a confirmation email from CLO. If you did not receive a cancellation confirmation email within 24 hours, it is your responsibility to promptly contact CLO to receive written confirmation otherwise your cancellation request will be considered invalid. If there are any conflicts between these terms and any other CLO terms, these terms will control.

Title: Human IK – Show Human IK Joint

Title: Human IK – Constrain Joint Translation
Content: Human IK - Constrain Joint Translation - Fix the selected joint to minimize the modification when other joints are moved. - For organic movement, the selected joint may not completely be constrained. - Select the Avatar joint to be constrained and click the Constrain Joint Translation icon from the Human IK window. - The constrained joint will turn grey and the alphabet T will hover over the joint.

Title: AI Avatar Studio (ver. 2024.1)
Content: List of Contents Open Face Image Render and Result Image Objective Generate photorealistic artwork by compositing an AI-created or any portrait photo onto a realistically rendered garment. Please note that AI Avatar Studio is being piloted as a Beta service, and may be suspended to provide better service. Location Main Menu Render AI Avatar Studio (Beta) Render Window Toolbar AI Avatar Studio (Beta) Operation Open Click the tool/menu in the Location. The AI Avatar Studio window appears. Face Image Generate a face image to be composited by entering prompts or upload it directly. Prompt Click the Prompt tab at the top of the AI Avatar Studio window. Set the options, enter the prompt, and then click the Generate button. Options Gender Set the gender of the avatar. Age Set the age range of the portrait to be generated. Ethnicity Set the ethnicity of the portrait to be generated. Text Prompt Enter the prompts. Writing Tips: List the words. Listing the desired words rather than long descriptive sentences can generate more effective results. Emphasize certain words more. If parentheses are used around a word you want to emphasize, it carries more weight. Weight increase rate: (word) 1.1 times, ((word)) 1.21 times. Maintain Prompt Even if the same prompts are used, the AI Face image is created anew each time. Thus, clicking the Maintain Prompt button may update the prompts while preserving the existing results as much as possible. The results may differ from the existing ones depending on the addition or change of the prompts. Random Sample prompts are provided randomly History Previously generated images and prompts are recorded in history, which is maintained only until CLO software is closed. Image Click the Image tab at the top of the AI Avatar Studio window. Click the Upload button to load a face image that fits the following guidelines: A close-up image of the front of the face with no parts covered by hair or shadows A photo with a natural facial expression, no accessories covering the face, and no visible teeth. A photo with a resolution of 1080 pixels or higher. A photo with even lighting, no strong light, and no mirrors in the background. Render and Result Image Note: In the CLO render window, when you run AI Avatar Studio immediately after the Final Render, it is automatically applied as a Target Image, which is more accurately analyzed and composited into a high-quality resulting image. Click the Upload button next to Target Image to load the render image to be composited. For more accurate analysis and results, it is recommended to use an image that fits the following guidelines: High-resolution image (2160 to 4320 pixels recommended) Well-focused and sharp image Image with good contrast between objects and background. Consistent lighting Appropriately sized image Click the Generate Button. The face image is composited into the render image, preserving the original garments, and then the resulting image is displayed. It may take a while to create when there are many users at the same time. Click the Save button to set the file name and path. The Result Image is saved.

Title: Human IK
Content: List of Contents Definition of Human IK Human IK Use Human IK Definition of Human IK - Avatar joints are organically linked that joints move naturally when modifying one particular joint, allowing easier pose modification process. Human IK - Hover over the second icon in the Vertical View Toggle Menu to view Avatar Display options. - Select the Show X-ray Joints icon. - The Human IK window will appear on the right top corner of the 3D window. Use Human IK Move Joints - Avatar joints will appear in yellow-green on the Avatars elbows, knees, and more. - Click and drag the desired Avatar joint to modify the pose. Rotate Joints - When the Avatar joint is clicked once, the Gizmo tool will appear. - Use the circles of the Gizmo tool to rotate joint and modify the pose.

Title: Material Type
Content: Objective Starting from CLO ver4.0.0, fabric gloss and hardware material can be adjusted with Type setting in the Property Editor. Location Object Browser Fabric Property Editor Material Type Operation Follow the indicated guideline below: Object Browser Fabric Property Editor Material Type Refer to the table below to adjust fabric gloss and hardware material. Name Description Type Choose the reflection type to express fabric gloss more realistically as needed. Fabric_Matte Reflection is adjusted optimal to express general fabric. Fabric_Shiny Reflection is adjusted optimal to express shiny fabric. Fabric_Silk/Satin (ver4.1.0) Reflection is adjusted optimal to express silk or satin fabric. Fabric_Velvet (ver4.1.0) Reflection is adjusted optimal to express velvet fabric. Fur_(Render Only) (ver4.2.0) Express realistic fur. Gem (Render Only) (ver5.0.0) Express gem material. Gem material is similar with glass, but expresses light reflection in multiple color. Adjust the opacity with the Absorption value. Lower the value is, more transparent the object is. The Absorption value is relative to the object's thickness. Thicker the object is, lower the Absorption value should be. Adjust the Abbe value to increase or reduce light reflection effect. Glass (ver4.1.0) Reflection is adjusted optimal to express glass materials. Adjust the opacity with the Absorption value. Lower the value is, more transparent the object is. The Absorption value is relative to the object's thickness. Thicker the object is, lower the Absorption value should be. Glitter (Render Only) (ver5.0.0) Express glitter. Light (Render Only) (ver5.0.0) Use garments or objects as lights. Adjust the brightness with the Color Mult option. Higher the value is, brighter the light is. As the light gets brighter, the color of the light deviates from the one set by the user. Leather Reflection is adjusted optimal to express leathers. Metal Reflection is adjusted optimal to express metallic materials. Plastic Reflection is adjusted optimal to express plastics. Skin (Render Only) (ver 6.0) Render human skin more realistically. Light enters an object and scatters beneath its surface. Not all light reflects from a surface. The objects penetrating lights such as leaves, fruits, or candles also be used for this. Note: When using Skin, you should not use a displacement map since the compatibility issue with V-Ray. Roughness Intensity Edit fabric gloss by adjusting Intensity of the Roughness. Map Edit fabric gloss by adding and modifying Roughness Map. Map Select the Browse button next to the Map option to add a Roughness Map to the selected Fabric style. Map Intensity Adjust the Map's Intensity. Invert Select to invert the gloss of the fabric. When this option is selected, shinny part becomes dull and vice-versa. To use Specular Maps provided in CLO below ver4.0.0, check this option. Reflection Intensity Greater the Reflection Intensity value is, more reflective the material or fabric is and vice-versa.

Title: Flatten
Content: Extract Patterns based on lines and shapes created on an Avatar. Note: The Flattening function only extracts closed shapes as Patterns. Since version 2024.2, the 2D pattern position and rotation are more aligned with the pattern placement on the 3D avatar. It is recommended to use CLO avatar for extracting the ideal pattern with front and back positions in the 2D window. When using a non-CLO avatar (eg. FBX) or missing the avatar, it is possible to lead to a non-ideal pattern position in the 2D window. Click on the Flatten tool. Points no longer appear and only lines appear on the Avatar. Hover the mouse over the shape to be extracted as Pattern. Select all areas to be extracted by holding Shift on the keyboard, then clicking on the desired areas. Hit Enter on the keyboard. The selected areas on the Avatar are converted to patterns and appear in both the 3D and 2D windows. Sewing lines are automatically established for adjacent Patterns.

Title: Userpool Settings
Content: New in 2024.2 List of Contents Concept Instruction FAQ Concept What is Userpool? A Userpool is a list of Members authorized to use the Owner's license. The license Owner can add or delete Members' email(CLO-SET account) who are allowed to use the license. Once the Member is added to the Userpool, Members can sign in to the software using their own CLO-SET account to use the Owner's license. By doing so, the Owner no longer needs to share the license ID and password, enhancing security and collaboration efficiency. Who can use Userpool? Any users with the licenses to sign in to CLO Network Onlineauth 2024.2 and later versions. Where is Userpool provided? The Userpool and a more detailed manual are provided in License Account Admin. Below is how you can access to the Userpool Settings page. Sign in clo3d.com &gt Click Account( ) on the top right side &gt Sign in &gt Click on the left side Instruction How to ADD members to the Userpool From the Userpool Settings Click and type the Member's email address. For better management, you can set a Member name when adding a member. The Member will receive an invitation email with the software installer included. From the Software (Auto Add) If the CLO-SET account is signed in from the software, the account will be automatically added as a Member to the Userpool list. The Owner will receive the notification email when the new Member is auto added. If the Owner doesn't want the Members to be auto added, Auto Add option can be turned off. How to DELETE members from the Userpool Mark the Members from the list &gt Click Deleted Members cannot sign in to the software with their CLO-SET account to use the Owner's license. Deleted Members can be added again whenever it's needed. FAQ Can the license Owner be the Member of the other Userpool? Yes. If the Owner's email has the CLO-SET account and that same account is invited to another Userpool, the account can also be a Member under another Userpool. I am invited as a Userpool Member, but cannot sign in to the software. The Member needs to be signed up to CLO-SET and have a CLO-SET account to sign in to the software. However, any email can be added when the Owner invites the Members. Do the Userpool Owner and Member related to the CLO-SET group's admin and users(collaborator, editor, viewer)? No, the Userpool is a separate feature from CLO-SET group permissions.

Title: CLO system requirements (June 2024)
Content: In this document, CLO or CLO software refers only to the CLO software installed on the user's local computer, and does not refer to CLO-SET and various other CLO products. Windows Category Minimum Recommended (Best Build) OS Windows 10 64-bit ( 1903 or later) Windows 10 64-bit (22H2 or later) 1) 2) 3) Windows 11 64-bit (23H2 or later) Processor AMD Ryzen 5 1500X Intel Core-i5 6400 AMD Ryzen 7/9 7000 series or higher Intel Core-i7/i9 14th Gen or higher Memory 8GB 32GB or more 4) Graphics card NVIDIA GeForce GTX 960 or NVIDIA Quadro P2200 NVIDIA GeForce RTX series or NVIDIA Quadro RTX , RTX A series 5) 6) 7) Storage HDD 10GB or more SSD 20GB or more Screen 1920x1080(FHD) 2560x1440(QHD), 3840x2160(UHD, 4K) Input device 3-button mouse 3-button mouse Network Internet connection required Internet connection required 1) Windows updates and patches are highly recommended. Windows Update - Microsoft Support 2) If dll-related errors occur while installing or running CLO, install the latest Microsoft Visual C++ Redistributable. X64 architecture is recommended. Microsoft Visual C++ Redistributable latest supported downloads 3) CLO software cannot run on Windows 10/11 N which media features removed. Download and install the Media Feature Pack from the Microsoft website. Media Feature Pack for Windows 10/11 N (February 2023) 4) For smoother operation, 16GB or more of memory is recommended. 32GB or more of memory is recommended if you are using multiple software at the same time and/or dealing with huge and complex garments. 5) CLO utilizes Nvidia CUDA acceleration technology for CLO GPU-Simulation and Rendering. So computers with only Intel Graphics or AMD graphics card do not benefit from GPU acceleration that speeds up CLO simulation and rendering. 6) For graphics card related issues, please see the following guide. In particular, please update your graphics card driver to the latest. Graphics Card Problems and Troubleshooting 7) A GPU that supports OpenGL Compatibility Profile 1.2 or higher is required to run CLO software. Some mobile GPU processors from AMD and Intel may not fully support openGL, which is essential for running CLO software, and may not run CLO software. If you are using a laptop or graphics card with a built-in CPU, check with the hardware manufacturer for the GPU model and whether it supports openGL. Mac Category Minimum Recommended (Best Build) Mac models All Macs released after 2015 1) Intel-chip Macs released after 2018 2) Apple Silicon Macs: M1, M2, M3 macOS Monterey 12 *For macOS dependencies, check out the notes below 3) Ventura 13, Sonoma 14 Processor Intel Core-i5 4cores Apple Silicon 4) Memory 8GB 24GB or more Storage HDD 10GB or more SSD 20GB or more Screen 1280x800 Retina 4K, Retina 5K supported 5) Input devices 3-button mouse 3-button mouse Network Internet connection required Internet connection required 1) Starting with CLO v2024, the minimum macOS has been changed to Monterey 12. See which macs are compatible with macOS Monterey 12 here. macOS Monterey is compatible with these computers. 2) Intel chip macs do not have Nvidia graphics cards, so mac users cannot make use of GPU acceleration, but simulation and rendering are supported normally. 3) macOS dependencies Sierra 10.12: users can install and run up to CLO 5.2. High Sierra 10.13: users can install and run up to CLO 6.1. Mojave 10.14: users can install and run up to CLO 6.2. Catalina 10.15: users can install and run up to CLO 7.3. Please note that CLO 7.0 and future versions will not run on macOS Mojave or earlier. 4) As of CLO 7.0, provides as a compatible build for both Apple Silicon macs and Intel chip macs. If you want to use version 6.2 or lower on Apple Silicon Mac, you need to install Apple Rosetta. Visit here for more info. If you need to install Rosetta on your Mac: Apple Support 5) CLO software supports Retina 5K and higher resolutions. However, it may run a bit slower in a resolution environment of 5K or higher. This is a known issue and is being improved. Additional Info CLO software does not support BootCamp in macOS. CLO software can be installed and run in virtual server environments such as Virtual Machine and Virtual Desktop Infrastructure and in cloud services. However, in this case, the CLO team does not provide technical support. CLO software does not support Apple iOS, iPad OS, tvOS, Android OS, Windows Mobile and Linux. CLO software does not support 32-bit OS (e.g. Windows 7 32-bit). CLO software can be downloaded as .exe or .dmg file format. It is not distributed in .msi or .pkg file format.

Title: Quadrangular/Triangular Mesh
Content: Convert synchronized 3D Garments into quadrangular or triangular mesh structures. Note: Please refer below explanation on different usages of Quadrangular Mesh versus Triangular Mesh. As the program speed may differ due to the difference in their intrinsic characteristics, please select most appropriate Mesh Type based on your needs. To use our program most efficiently, however, we strongly suggest you to set all Pattern Mesh to Triangular when editing 3D Garments, and then change ONLY necessary Patterns' Mesh type to Quadrangular to complete the Garment. When to Use Triangular Mesh: All Cases, except for special cases needed to use Quadrangular Mesh. When to Use Quadrangular Mesh: When a detail of 3D Garment needs to round smoothly such as shirts collar or piping. Click the pattern in 2D or 3D window. Change the Mesh Type to the Quad (Otimized) in the Property Editor.

Title: Avatar Properties
Content: Set the properties of the avatar. Click an avatar with Select/Move tool. Click an avatar. The properties appear in the Property Editor. Adjust each properties below as needed. Properties Description Information Name / Item NO. Enter a name and an item number of the avatar. Tech Pack (CLO-SET) Set whether to include avatar in the Tech Pack or not. Body Styling Style Configurator Set the appearance of the avatar. You can manually set the color of hair, skin, underwear, eyebrows, Eye (ver 2024.1) and lips by clicking the Style Configurator button on the right. Eye Control (ver 7.2 ) Adjust the position of the avatar's eyes horizontally or vertically. Note: This option is only supported for the new avatars available starting with version 7.2. Surface Skin Offset Adjust the distance between the avatar and the garment. Since the avatar and the garment consist of the meshes, a very high value of particle distance and low value of Skin Offset can cause the avatar to protrude out from under the garment. To prevent this, the default Skin Offset value is set to 3mm, which is the proper value for creating a garment. When you fit your garment accurately or create a fitted garment, lower the value of the Skin Offset. Note: Leave the default value until you almost finish your garment, since the simulation is being slow when you lower the Skin Offset of the avatar and the Particle Distance of the garment. Friction Increase the friction value to prevent a garment slipped away while draping or animating. Static The friction when a garment is in stationary position. Kinetic The friction when a garment is moving. Soft Body Simulation Apply deformable body simulation to express skin elasticity This option is only available on CLO's default adult avatar, and can only be simulated with garments. Note:Soft body simulation is reflected when recording animation to enable realistic expression, and soft body simulation can also be applied to 3D dummy or scan files converted to CLO avatars. (ver 7.3 ) Divide Mesh Adjust the number of the avatar's meshes to smooth the surface of the avatar. Be aware to use this feature when it is necessary. The higher you set the meshes, the bigger the size of the file can cause the slower speed of the program. E.g. This works best when you drape a fitted garment such as leggings since the meshes of the avatar appear. Material Set the Material of the avatar.

Title: Seamline Puckering
Content: List of Contents Seamline Puckering Create Puckering Seamline Puckering - Create Puckering to seamlines. - Select the Seamline Puckering tool from the 2D toolbar. - Or, navigate to the Main Menu and select Material Puckering Seamline Puckering. Title: [Tool] Seam Line Puckering
Content: Objective Apply Puckering to Pattern's seamlines. Title: Steam
Content: Objective Shrink or stretch Fabric partially like as using a steam iron. Location Main Menu Materials Steam Steam 2D Toolbar Steam Operation Steam Setting Follow the indicated guideline below: Main Menu Materials Steam Steam 2D Toolbar Steam All Patterns are now being displayed in mesh. The Steam Brush appears at the top-left corner of the 2D window. Set the value as desired. Shrinkage Sets the shrinkage level. Size Sets the size of the brush. Hardness Sets the hardness of the steam. Click and drag on desired area to steam. According to the shrinkage, the selected area is now being displayed in light-blue or orange. Activate the Simulate. Remove Steam Follow the indicated guideline below: Main Menu Materials Steam Steam 2D Toolbar Steam Right-click on a pattern to remove steam, and select either Remove Steam on Selected Pattern or Remove All Steam. The steam is now being deleted accordingly. Note: It can also be removed from the same right-click pop-up menu with Edit Pattern or Transform Pattern tools.

Title: Fold/Sew Pleats
Content: Objective Create a variety of pleats, fold and sew them (ver2.3.0). Location Main Menu 2D Pattern Pleats Pleats Fold / Pleats Sewing 2D Toolbar Pleats Fold / Pleats Sewing Operation Pleats Fold Select the tool/menu indicated in Location. Click to establish the initial point for the direction of the pleats, then double-click to establish the end point. Pleats Fold window appears. Select a desired type of pleats. Depending on the selected pleats type, the Fold Angles of the Internal Lines are now being highlighted. Note: Yellow: Outside fold line (Fold angle of zero(0) degree), Light-blue: Inside fold line (Fold angle of 360 degree), Not highlighted: No fold line (Fold angle of 180 degree) Check the Reverse Direction option as needed. The direction of pleats being folded are now being reversed. Click OK button to complete. Pleats Sewing Select the tool/menu indicated in Location. Click on the initial point and drag up to the end point of the seamline on the pleats Pattern. Note: In case of sewing the pleat pattern only, press enter to proceed to the next step. (ver 6.0) On the pleats Pattern, click on the first Sewing Line to begin with, and move the mouse to the end point. Sewing is now being established for every three(3) segments (the amount of segments needed to create each individual pleat). Click on the end point to complete. The color of the fluorescent sewing lines are now being changed for respective seam color, indicating that the sewing is being completed.

Title: Pattern Annotation
Content: List of Contents Pattern Annotation Adding Pattern Annotation Editing Pattern Annotation Pattern Annotation - Create and edit Pattern Annotation on Patterns in the 2D Window. - Select the Pattern Annotation tool from the 2D toolbar. Adding Pattern Annotation - Select the Pattern Annotation tool from the 2D toolbar and navigate to the 2D Window. - Hover over the Pattern that Pattern Annotation will be added on. Click once or click and drag to create Pattern Annotation. - A marquee box will appear. Type in contents. - Click on the Pattern or hit Ctrl + Enter on the keyboard to complete the entry. - Established Pattern Annotation will appear in blue texts. EditingPattern Annotation - Select the Pattern Annotation tool from the 2D toolbar and navigate to the 2D Window. - Click on the Pattern Annotation to be edited as it will be re-activated for editing. - Revise the annotation as needed. - When completed, click once on a Pattern or hit Ctrl + Enter on the keyboard.

Title: Move/Delete Pattern Annotation
Content: List of Contents Move Delete Objective Move or delete Pattern annotations on Patterns. Location 2D Toolbar Select/Move Pattern Annotation Operation Move/ Rotate (ver 5.2) Click the tool indicated in Location. Click and drag the annotation to the desired place. The annotation is moved. Or, drag after clicking the annotation's pivot point towards the direction the annotation should rotate to. (ver 5.2) The annotation is rotated. Delete Click the tool indicated in Location. Right-click on the Pattern annotation to be deleted. The pop-up menu appears. Select Delete. The selected Pattern annotation is deleted. Note: You can also delete the Pattern annotation by hitting the Delete key on the keyboard.

Title: Can I change my subscription plan?
Content: You can change the plan at least 24 hours before the next bill due to your current plan. To change the subscription plan from monthly to yearly (or vice versa), Sign in to the CLO web and go to the Subscription page. Click the "Change Plan" button. Check the current subscription and plan type that will be changed. Click the "Change" button. *Once you change your subscription plan, you can only change the plan again ONLY AFTER you complete purchasing the product on the starting date of the changed plans. Until then, you cannot cancel the changes. Only canceling a subscription is available. *If you change the plan, you will be charged the amount for the changed plan from the next payment date of the existing plan. *If you cancel the subscription, you cannot change the plan type. *Individual plans cannot be changed as student plans and vice versa. To change your license from CLO for Individuals to CLO for Business, please reach out to CLO via Contact Us.
